A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TIR-Agent study, with inspectable text, equations, five tables and seven figures. Neither contains an appendix. v2 mentions supplementary material, but that material is not included and cannot establish additional changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration experiments on MiO100, including baseline comparisons, out-of-domain evaluations, ablations and training analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including restoration quality, inference times, ablations and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The Qwen3-VL-8B agent, SFT/RL pipeline, exploration-driven perturbation, adaptive reward and globally shared model-call pool retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-derived training images and the same MiO100 evaluations: Groups A–C, the five-combination SimpleCall comparison, and unseen degradation combinations with D=2 and D≥3.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in all corresponding tables, including SimpleCall variants and the three proprietary models. Correcting 'Claude Pous' to 'Claude Opus' in the prose does not introduce a different comparator.

E3.justification: Training sample counts, model size, budgets, rollout settings and six evaluation metrics are unchanged. The Figure 7 caption correction from alpha_t to alpha_m identifies the existing tool-perturbation experiment rather than changing its setting.

E4.justification: The included ablations, exploration analyses, reward curves, hyperparameter sweeps, proprietary-model analyses and qualitative examples are unchanged. v2 adds a supplementary-analysis pointer but includes no additional analysis supporting it.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The eight rollouts per training sample remain unchanged and do not constitute newly reported independent experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the five matched tables are unchanged, as are the plotted results and qualitative examples. For example, Table 1 retains Group A PSNR 22.07 and runtime 61.58 seconds; Table 4 retains D=2 PSNR 23.19.

T1.justification: The finite-horizon decision formulation and Equations (1)–(9) defining perturbation and adaptive rewards are mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about learned tool orchestration, EDP, MAR, training infrastructure, superiority over 12 baselines and over 2.5× inference speedup.

C2.justification: Interpretations of exploration collapse, competing quality metrics, proprietary-model task/tool biases, generalization and hyperparameter tradeoffs remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: The same learning rates, epochs, batch sizes, GPU allocations, concurrency limits, retry mechanism and data filtering information are disclosed. v2's supplementary-material pointers provide no additional technical details or concrete access instructions within the supplied PDF.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 58 works and retain the same research positioning, including the distinction from SimpleCall. Reference formatting and an author-name diacritic differ without changing cited-work identity.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar, spelling and erroneous Figure 4 references to Figure 7. It also revises author order, contribution markers and affiliations, removes keywords and adds acknowledgements. The substantive prose and section sequence remain largely identical.

P2.justification: v2 substantially changes typography, margins, headers and float placement, including wrapping prose around the SimpleCall and ablation tables. Figures 2/3 and Tables 2/3 exchange numbers. Displays become markedly smaller, and the SimpleCall and Figure 7 captions receive labeling corrections.

improvement.justification: v2 usefully corrects misleading figure references and caption labels, but its layout reduces numerical table text from roughly 8–9 points to 5–6 points, particularly affecting the SimpleCall and ablation comparisons. This makes the unchanged evidence harder to inspect at normal page size. The readability loss outweighs the limited editorial gains.
